summary: Saturday card, researched 8:15 to 8:45 AM ET with the first published v2 forecasts (12:11Z). Two picks: Texas A&M -16.5 and Duke -10, both on availability reports plus the model. Maryland +3 was dropped after reports that its top two running backs are in doubt. Five other model leans stay on watch because no sourced reason beyond v2 supports them; every Week 3 game is a thin sample and v2 has not beaten the closing line.

gamePicks.title: Texas A&M -16.5 vs Kentucky
gamePicks.quoteNote: DraftKings' line and price as relayed by ESPN's odds feed at that time; not re-read at the DraftKings app. Check the price before following.
gamePicks.edge: v2 home margin 28.6 (80% range 7.7 to 49.5). Chance of home -16.5: 77.1%, against 54.1% break-even at -118: +22.9 points, +0.424u per unit. Normal approximation from the stored v2 range; not calibrated at this line.
gamePicks.cutoff: HOME -16.5 at -118 or better. Closed to new entries on no key number, or at -133 or worse at -16.5.
gamePicks.why: Kentucky's Friday SEC availability report lists five players out: TE Lincoln Watkins, OL Jay Clark, DB Andre Clarke Jr., DB Grant Grayton and DL Jamarrion Harkless. That is a thinner line and secondary for an offense that managed 209 yards and three turnovers against Alabama last week (17-45). Texas A&M is 2-0: 50-0 over Missouri State and 48-20 over Arizona State with four takeaways. v2 has the home margin at 28.6 against a 16.5 line, the largest FBS-vs-FBS gap on the slate that is not a huge underdog.
gamePicks.risk: 16.5 is a lot of points. A&M's offense had only 255 yards against Arizona State and won on turnovers; RB Jamarion Morrow and WR Ashton Bethel-Roman are doubtful for A&M. v2's number leans on two games, one of them a 50-0 over a weak opponent, so treat its 77% as a direction, not a probability. A late Kentucky score can steal the cover.
gamePicks.availabilityNote: Indiana permits wagers on college sides and totals and DraftKings operates there; this is a full-game side on the DraftKings board.

gamePicks.cutoff: HOME -10 at -105 or better. Closed to new entries on no key number, or at -120 or worse at -10.
gamePicks.why: Stanford's ACC injury report lists twelve players out, including four cornerbacks (Jason Hill Jr., Chris Garland, Breylan Thompson, Jack Duckworth), safety Zaiden McDonald, two defensive linemen and three offensive linemen. Stanford scored 6 on 299 yards against Miami. Duke is 2-0, held Tulane to 3 and won at Illinois 31-27 as a 6-point underdog. v2 has the home margin at 19.1 against a 10-point line.
gamePicks.risk: Duke has three offensive linemen out (Jacobowitz, McCranie, Fina) and a fourth questionable, and scored only 17 against Tulane; if Stanford controls the line of scrimmage this stays close. Stanford gets WR Nico Brown and OL Simione Pale back. Both teams have two games of history, so v2's margin is a thin read.
